title: Ephemeral service accounts, delegated ownership and automated audit hooks
creator: Sana Iqbal
description:
Goal: Design and implement a hardened admin surface for service accounts focusing on ephemeral account creation, delegated ownership with TTLs, templated least-privilege manifests, and wired audit events for traceability. This ticket scopes the engineering work for: 1) a declarative template format (YAML) for creating service accounts with attached policies and TTLs; 2) ownership delegation model that allows owners to be ephemeral (group or person) with automated transfer/expiration and an approval flow that integrates with SSO/SAML groups; 3) enforcement hooks into RBAC v2 policy engine so templates are validated at creation time (policy-as-code checks) and rejected if overly permissive; 4) structured audit event schema and forwarding to our audit pipeline (Cloud Logging + SIEM) including correlation IDs for lifecycle events; 5) CLI and Console UX changes to create, rotate, and revoke ephemeral service accounts; 6) migration strategy for existing long-lived service accounts into the new model (discovery + gradual swap).

Security constraints and design choices: prefer ephemeral by-default (short TTLs), default to least-privilege role bindings derived from template inference, require at least one owner and an automated escalation path (if owner leaves, a scoped team admin is notified and an auto-delegation window begins). KMS/HSM key binding for long-lived keys is out-of-scope for sprint but included in follow-up. Integration points: RBAC v2 policy engine (OPA-backed), SSO provider (SAML/SCIM) for owner groups, Audit pipeline (structured JSON events with "sa_event_type", "actor", "correlation_id", "before", "after").

Success criteria: - Template schema v1 published and validated by policy checks - Console + CLI flows for creating ephemeral SA working end-to-end in staging - Audit events emitted for create/transfer/rotate/revoke and visible in our SIEM dashboards - Migration plan and a pilot migration of 10 low-risk SAs completed
